name: MA-03
label: Safe D

key_factors: Trahan's roughly 200-to-1 fundraising edge ($1.8M cash vs. $7K) leaves Grossi unable to compete
District's D+11 partisan lean in deep-blue Massachusetts
Incumbent Trahan running for re-election with no serious contest on record
Prediction markets price a Democratic win near 97%
model.rationale: Every available signal points the same way: the district's D+11 lean, Trahan's incumbency, and an overwhelming money advantage over a challenger who has raised under $10,000. Markets price this near 97% Democratic, and nothing in the record suggests a competitive race.
model.watch: A late wave of Republican outside spending or an unusually strong GOP national environment could narrow the margin, though flipping the seat would require a historic shift.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Massachusetts' third district leans Democratic by about eleven points, and incumbent Lori Trahan is seeking another term from a commanding financial position. She has raised roughly $1.9 million and holds $1.8 million on hand, while Republican Gary Grossi has raised about $9,000. An independent candidate is also on the ballot but shows no reported fundraising. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, though prediction markets price a Democratic win near 97%.

The fundamentals all point in one direction: the district's partisan lean, Trahan's incumbency, and the enormous spending gap favor her. A national environment tilted toward Republicans could shave a few points off the margin, but a deficit of more than twenty points would be needed to put the seat in play. The race rates Safe Democratic, with moderate confidence given the absence of polling.
